title: Subrogation and Recovery Bulletin: Rental Money Recovered under Cardinal Rental Reimbursement
content:
**Recovery position for Cardinal Rental Reimbursement.** When the other party is at fault, the rental paid under the option is part of Cardinal's subrogation demand.

Rental money comes back in one of two ways, and the two have different effects on the claim:

| Recovery source | Rental benefit paid on the option | Per-loss benefit and days on the claim |
|---|---|---|
| Subrogation recovery from the at-fault party's insurer | Lowered by the amount recovered | Not given back: neither benefit nor days are restored |
| Agency credit for an overbilled invoice | Lowered by the amount credited | The credited amount is given back to the per-loss benefit |

A recovery is recorded once per payment and source.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical figures, Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 50/1500, $1500.00 per-loss maximum)

Agency payments of $600.00 have been made on the claim, so rental benefit paid is $600.00 and $900.00 of the per-loss benefit remains.

- **Subrogation recovery of $200.00 from the other insurer.** Rental benefit paid falls to $400.00. The per-loss benefit still available stays at $900.00, and the days used on the claim do not change.
- **Agency credit of $50.00 against an overbilled invoice.** Rental benefit paid falls by a further $50.00. The per-loss benefit still available rises by $50.00.

## Points of judgement

- *Two recoveries from different sources against the same payment.* Each is recorded, because the once-only rule is per payment and per source.
- *A second subrogation recovery entry against the same payment.* Not recorded again: a subrogation recovery against that payment is already on record.
